answer:
Simulate a 2D lid-driven cavity flow in the x-y plane.
The cavity is 0.1 m by 0.1 m in x and y and one cell thick in z.
The z-thickness is 0.01 m, with the front and back boundaries set to empty.
Use icoFoam, the OpenFOAM incompressible laminar finite volume solver with PISO pressure-velocity coupling.
Set the application in system/controlDict to icoFoam.
Create three boundary patches named movingWall, fixedWalls, and frontAndBack.
Use a uniform Cartesian mesh of 20 by 20 by 1 cells.
Define the blockMeshDict block vertices at (0 0 0), (0.1 0 0), (0.1 0.1 0), (0 0.1 0) and extrude 0.01 m in z.
Set the block grading to uniform, with 20 cells in x, 20 cells in y, and 1 cell in z.
The resulting cell size is 0.005 m in x and y.
Set the kinematic viscosity nu to 0.001 m²/s in transportProperties.
The Reynolds number is 100 based on lid speed 1 m/s, cavity size 0.1 m, and nu 0.001 m²/s.
Set startTime to 0 in system/controlDict.
Set endTime to 0.5 s, deltaT to 0.002 s, writeControl to timeStep, and writeInterval to 20.
The solution is written every 20 time steps, i.e. every 0.04 s of simulated time.
Set the initial internal field for U to uniform (0 0 0).
Set the initial internal field for p to uniform 0.
Set the U boundary condition on movingWall, the top wall at y = 0.1 m, to fixedValue uniform (1 0 0), so the lid moves to the right at 1 m/s.
Set the U boundary condition on fixedWalls, the left, right, and bottom walls, to noSlip.
Set the U boundary condition on frontAndBack to empty.
Set the p boundary condition on movingWall and fixedWalls to zeroGradient.
Set the p boundary condition on frontAndBack to empty.
Use the standard icoFoam cavity tutorial settings for fvSchemes and fvSolution.
